ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: NVDA appeared in all 19 overnight screens — the strongest consensus signal of the batch. The stock enters its Aug 26 earnings at a multi-year valuation low (~25x forward P/E vs. a historical pre-earnings norm of 35-40x), while revenue estimates have been revised up 6.67% in the past 3 months and the company itself guided $91B in Q2 revenue against a consensus now at $92-94B. With $600B+ in hyperscaler capex underpinning demand and Alphabet/Amazon both raising AI infrastructure budgets, a beat-and-raise scenario could drive a significant multiple re-rating; a re-rate to just 30x forward would imply 20%+ upside from current levels. Defined-risk call spreads (Aug 29 or Sep expiry) are preferred over outright stock given post-earnings volatility history and the binary nature of the print.
ideas.catalyst: Q2 FY2027 earnings report confirmed for August 26, 2026 after market close — 6 days away
ideas.edge: 68-analyst consensus price target of $303.09 vs. ~$225 current price implies ~35% upside gap; stock trades at ~25x forward P/E vs. historical pre-earnings range of 35-40x; revenue estimates revised up 6.67% over 3 months; sector sold off ~5% this week creating a cheaper entry ahead of print
ideas.bull_case: A beat-and-raise on Aug 26 with Q3 guidance above $95B re-rates the stock toward 30-35x forward earnings, driving 20-35% upside; hyperscaler capex tailwinds from Alphabet ($195-205B) and Amazon ($220B) confirm multi-year demand visibility.
ideas.bear_case: Post-earnings volatility is historically severe for NVDA; a guidance miss or margin disappointment in a hawkish macro environment could flush the stock further below the 25x floor; elevated implied volatility makes outright long calls expensive.

ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc. (ADR)
ideas.thesis: SKHY appeared in all 19 overnight screens alongside NVDA, reflecting unanimous conviction on the AI memory supply chain angle. Options offer defined-risk entry if IV permits.

ideas.edge: Bank of America $250 price target vs. ~$155-165 current price implies ~55% upside; $29B buyback commits >50% of FCF (2025-2027) to shareholder returns; stock is ~12% below Nasdaq debut price despite 76% operating margin and 108% YoY net income growth
